questions.question: Find the second quartile (median) of the 7 data values 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.
questions.explanation: The middle of 7 values is the 4th from the smallest. So the answer is 7.

questions.question: Find the first quartile of the 7 data values 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.
questions.explanation: The first quartile is the median of the lower half 2, 4, 5, which is below the median (7). So the answer is 4.

questions.question: Find the third quartile of the 7 data values 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.
questions.explanation: The third quartile is the median of the upper half 9, 11, 13, which is above the median (7). So the answer is 11.

questions.question: Find the second quartile (median) of the 8 data values 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 14.
questions.explanation: The middle of 8 values is the average of the 4th and 5th values. (6+8)÷2=7.

questions.question: Find the first quartile of the 8 data values 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 14.
questions.explanation: The first quartile is the median of the lower half 1, 3, 4, 6. The middle of 4 values is the average of the 2nd and 3rd values: (3+4)÷2=3.5.

questions.question: For a data set, the first quartile is 5 and the third quartile is 12. Find the interquartile range.
questions.explanation: Interquartile range = third quartile - first quartile = 12-5=7.

questions.question: Find the interquartile range of the 7 data values 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15.
questions.explanation: The first quartile is the median of the lower half 3, 5, 6, which is 5. The third quartile is the median of the upper half 10, 12, 15, which is 12. 12-5=7.

questions.question: Which range does the "box" part of a box plot represent?
choices: From the first quartile to the third quartile
From the minimum to the maximum
Around the mean
From the median to the maximum
questions.answer: From the first quartile to the third quartile
questions.explanation: The box represents the first quartile through the third quartile (about the middle 50% of the data). The whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum.

questions.question: In a box plot, what value does the vertical line drawn inside the box represent?
choices: Median
Mean
Mode
Minimum
questions.explanation: The vertical line inside the box represents the median (second quartile). Note that it is not the mean.

questions.question: Which value cannot be read from a box plot?
choices: Mean
Median
Maximum
First quartile
questions.explanation: A box plot shows five values (the five-number summary): the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, and maximum. However, the mean cannot be read from it.

questions.question: In a box plot, the minimum is 4 and the maximum is 20. Find the range of this data.
questions.explanation: Range = maximum - minimum = 20-4=16.

questions.question: In a box plot, the left edge of the box points to 6 and the right edge points to 14. Find the interquartile range.
questions.explanation: The left edge of the box is the first quartile and the right edge is the third quartile. 14-6=8.

questions.question: Out of all the data, about what percent falls inside the "box" of a box plot (from the first quartile to the third quartile)?
choices: About 50%
About 25%
About 75%
About 100%
questions.explanation: The quartiles divide the data into four equal parts, so the box contains about the middle 50%.

questions.question: Comparing the box plots of Class A and Class B, the box for Class A is wider. What can be concluded from this?
choices: Class A has a larger interquartile range
Class A has a larger mean
Class A has more students
Class A has a larger maximum
questions.answer: Class A has a larger interquartile range
questions.explanation: The width of the box represents the interquartile range. The wider it is, the greater the spread of the data around the center.

questions.question: Find the second quartile (median) of the 9 data values 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12.
questions.explanation: The middle of 9 values is the 5th value. So the answer is 6.

questions.question: Find the first quartile of the 9 data values 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12.
questions.explanation: This is the median of the lower half 1, 2, 4, 5, excluding the median (6). (2+4)÷2=3.

questions.question: Find the third quartile of the 9 data values 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12.
questions.explanation: This is the median of the upper half 8, 9, 11, 12, excluding the median (6). (9+11)÷2=10.

questions.question: Find the interquartile range of the 9 data values 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12.
questions.explanation: The third quartile is 10 and the first quartile is 3. 10-3=7.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct description of the interquartile range?
choices: It is not easily affected by extreme values (outliers)
It is the most easily affected by outliers
It equals the number of data values
It is always larger than the range
questions.answer: It is not easily affected by extreme values (outliers)
questions.explanation: The interquartile range uses only the middle 50% of the data, so it is not easily affected by extreme values at either end. The range, however, is strongly affected by outliers.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate feature of a box plot compared with a histogram?
choices: It makes it easy to line up and compare the distributions of several data sets
It shows the exact frequency of each class
The mean can be read from it
The number of data values can be determined
questions.answer: It makes it easy to line up and compare the distributions of several data sets
questions.explanation: Because a box plot is compact, it is well suited to lining up the data of several groups and comparing the position and spread of their distributions.
